memory_candidates.content: When deleting an experimental feature gated behind a numbered stage in a skill's SKILL.md (e.g. 'Stage 3.6'), expect the acceptance grep for the stage number to also hit unrelated agent files that happen to use the same numeral for their own internal stage sequence (e.g. an agent's own 'Stage 3.6: Observation Duty' or 'Stage 3.6: Handoff on Context Pressure'), plus every cross-file prose pointer into those agents' own stages. Treat this as one coherent false-positive class ('numbered-stage collision') rather than auditing each pointer individually as a new site.

When a large deletion/removal task's implementation dispatch is itself running inside an active /orchestrate cycle for the same task, a plan step calling for a live end-to-end /orchestrate smoke test on OTHER tasks should not be executed literally -- it risks session/task-lock contention with the running cycle. Prefer the plan's own dry-run-equivalent escape valve when offered: a parser-level or dispatch-args-level static smoke check (source the shared arg parser under `set -u` with representative multi-task/flag arguments; grep the dispatch-args strings for the removed tokens) plus corroborating green coverage from the existing automated test suite's orchestrate-mechanics tests.
